rho_reference_assessment.protocol: note section 9.15 (registered before code): on each GLS curve the matched walk is the <+-psi> walk, psi the GLS endomorphism (the twisted p^2-power Frobenius, psi^2 = -1), with 16 <+-psi>, 16 negation and 16 unfolded walks per curve; S_B / rho = total_muls / mean fp_muls of the 16 <+-psi> walks (set-up and class representatives included); the improvement compares arm A against the negation walk with arm B against the <+-psi> walk.
rho_reference_assessment.matches_protocol: every record carries 16 Gls, 16 negation and 16 unfolded walks, all correct, matched_fold = Gls; rho_matched_muls equals the mean of the Gls walks' fp_muls; both arms of a curve ran identical walks (checks above).
rho_reference_assessment.strongest_available: on all 10 curves j(E) is in F_{p^2} but not in F_p (independent Python check: j^(p^2) = j, j^p != j), so the only Frobenius-type endomorphism over F_{p^4} is psi from the p^2-power map (verified independently: psi^2(G) = -G, psi(G) = [lambda]G, lambda^2 = -1 mod n); Aut(E) = {+-1} (j != 0, 1728); <+-psi> (classes of 4) is the largest fold, no order-8 fold from a p-power map exists. <+-psi> walks take 0.47-0.79 sqrt(n) steps (16-walk means over the 10 curves; 0.54-0.61 at p = 397), against sqrt(pi n / 8) = 0.627 sqrt(n).
rho_reference_assessment.same_unit_and_process: one process per (p, seed) runs arm A, arm B and inside each arm's run the 16 + 16 + 16 walks (rho4_folded) on the same instance with the same Fp4/Curve4 counters.
rho_reference_assessment.unpriced_native_work: Read from src/cryptanalysis/quartic_folds.rs, klein_v4.rs, d4_weighted_s5.rs and gaudry_quartic.rs: the index calculus charges F_p multiplications only (the Fp4 counter: an F_{p^4} multiplication 19, an inversion 40; the solve's F_p multiplications counted directly; the matrix at 16 per mod-n multiplication). Unpriced on the index calculus: the Macaulay matrices' entry traffic and additions (emitted: macaulay_entries, rows x cols at each call's last degree), the solve's F_p inversions (inv_mod per pivot or eigenvector; count not emitted, at most one per pivot row, far fewer than the entries), hash and table work in the lift-back, F_p additions. Unpriced on the walks: per step the hash-table lookup and insert, the partition hashes (two with the look-ahead) and the class comparisons, F_p additions (emitted: steps). The protocol's band prices one GAE per Macaulay entry and one per walk step, GAE = the curve's measured F_p multiplications per affine addition (fp_muls_per_add = 97.0 on every record). Native work is unpriced on both arms, so the 0, 0.1 and 1 GAE values differ.
limitations: 16 walks per curve and fold: about 13 % sampling error on each walk mean; the per-curve improvement, a ratio of two walk means and two IC totals, carries it twice.

The <+-psi> walk applies psi to both coordinates on every step (152-154 F_p multiplications a step at p = 397, against 109 for the negation walk); comparing psi(x) first and mapping y only when needed would save an estimated 6 % (not measured). S_B / rho and the improvement are favourable to the index calculus by about that much.

Below n ~ 2^25 the walks' set-up dominates and the <+-psi> walk costs more F_p multiplications than the negation walk, which inflates the improvement at p <= 149; the README row quotes the improvement at p >= 197 only.

The two arms share one seeded RNG for target draws and Wiedemann; the target streams coincide until arm B's first Wiedemann attempt and then diverge, so the comparison is paired on a prefix of each stream only (code reading of collect_and_solve and Arm::attempt). This adds noise to S_A / S_B per curve, not a bias.
The handovers (2^93.2, 2^88.0) are section 11.16's model extrapolated with theory exponents from measured constants, not measured crossings.
